Sandbox_Crepuscular_NightMode_tooltip: How night is decided. Fixed hours: night runs between the two hours below, every day of the year, whatever the Day/Night Cycle setting. Seasonal night: the game's own dusk and dawn, which move with the seasons and follow the Day/Night Cycle setting (endless day has no night, endless night is always night).
Sandbox_Crepuscular_NightStartHour_toolt: Hour of the day, 0 to 23, at which night begins when Night mode is Fixed hours. Night can run past midnight. If both hours are the same there is no night at all, and the log says so.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_NightEndHour_tooltip: Hour of the day, 0 to 23, at which night ends when Night mode is Fixed hours.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Day_tooltip: What changes by day while no event runs. Fields are key=value, separated by ;. speed=+25 makes 25 percent of ordinary zombies one tier faster (shambler to fast shambler, fast shambler to sprinter) and speed=-50 makes 50 percent one tier slower; a zombie that speeds up is among the last to slow down, and speed=0 keeps every zombie at the game's speed. steps=2 moves them two tiers: always sprinters or always shamblers. health=0.7 gives new and reloaded zombies 70 percent of the health they roll and lowers any zombie above 70 percent of the most a new one can have; health=1.5 gives new and reloaded zombies 150 percent, and zombies already around keep theirs. rise=50 marks 50 percent of the zombies killed while the day lasts to get up again (rise=100 all of them, rise=0 none), and wake=true lets marked corpses get up while it lasts; a corpse marked by day without wake=true gets up once a definition with it applies, such as the default Night. When and how often they rise is set by the options below. speed, health, rise and the sky numbers can grow with the days since the world began: speed=+25..+75;grow=60d goes from +25 on world day 0 to +75 on world day 60 and stays there, grow=30d..90d moves it between those days instead, and health=0.7..0.4, rise=25..100 and fog=0.2..0.6 work the same way. World days are counted at noon, as for every= and mindays=, and a speed or rise share is rounded to a whole percent. A range needs grow= in the same definition, and grow= moves only that definition's own ranges. Monsters of every kind, Bandits and crawlers keep their own speed and are never capped; the health factor is given as the game creates a zombie, before it marks some of them, so a reloaded crawler or a new mutant may get it too. off=cof,mutants turns those monster kinds off (off=none turns none off): far ones are removed, The Mutants makes no new mutants and Cry of Fear Monster NPCs spawns nothing new. A kind no definition turns off is left alone. For Cry of Fear monsters only at night, write off=cof here and keep its own Night only option off; as with that option, each time cof is on again every Cry of Fear home may be filled again, so killed monsters come back too. set.Table.Option=value changes a sandbox option, for example set.ZombieLore.Toughness=1, or set.Option=value for an option without a table, for example set.HoursForCorpseRemoval=24; it goes back to its base value when the day ends. say=text shows a line to every player when the day begins (say=@Key shows that translation), and color=rrggbb gives its colour. sound=Name plays that game sound on every player's game at the same moment, with or without a line, for example sound=MetaWolfHowl; upper and lower case matter. A player who joins or loads the game while the day lasts gets the line and the sound then. sky=rrggbbaa tints the light while the day lasts, aa being the strength from 00 (none) to ff (full), for example sky=ff964660. fogcolor=rrggbb colours fog, and fog=, desat= (grey), dark= (night strength) and ambient= (ambient light) set those values from 0 to 1. Each replaces the game's own value while it applies and gives it back afterwards, and one not set stays the game's. The server sets them: in multiplayer players see a change with the next climate update, up to about 10 in-game minutes later, and fade it in. Admin climate overrides win, rain and storms still mix in their own sky and fog, and view distance can't change. A sun event starts from these values, except say=, color= and sound=. The default, speed=+25;health=0.7, makes a quarter of the zombies faster and the zombies more fragile, zombies killed by day stay down, and the sky is the game's. A bad field is skipped and logged, and the rest applies.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Night_tooltip: What changes by night while no event runs, written as for Day: speed=-50 or speed=+25, steps=2, health=1.5, rise=50, wake=true, a range that grows such as speed=-25..-75;grow=60d, off=mutants,cof or off=none, set.Table.Option=value, say=text, color=rrggbb, sound=Name, and the sky: sky=rrggbbaa, fogcolor=rrggbb and fog=, desat=, dark= and ambient= from 0 to 1, which reach players' games with the next climate update, up to about 10 in-game minutes later. The values go back to their base when the night ends. A moon event starts from these values except say=, color= and sound=, even when it runs into the day. The default, speed=-50;rise=50;wake=true;off=mutants, makes half of the zombies slower, marks half of the zombies killed at night to get up again and lets marked corpses get up at night, keeps The Mutants from making mutants at night and removes far mutants; the sky is the game's.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Events1_tooltip: Moons and suns: special nights and days. Events are separated by |, fields by ;. Each event needs id=name (letters a-z, digits and _) and track=moon (decided when night begins) or track=sun (decided when day begins). Conditions, which must all hold: moon=full (the first night of a full moon; also new, waxingcrescent, firstquarter, waxinggibbous, waninggibbous, thirdquarter, waningcrescent), date=10-31 or date=12-20..01-05, month=6..8, season=summer, every=30 (every 30 days since the world began; every=30+5 shifts it by 5), mindays=30 and maxdays=365 (days since the world began), nth=4 (every 4th time its calendar conditions hold), after=id (the first time after that event ended), cooldown=20d or 36h, interval=3d..7d (after each start it waits a random 3 to 7 whole days, counted in world days, before it can happen again, and the first wait counts from world day 0, the day mindays= and every= count from, or for hours from 07:00 that day; interval=7d waits exactly 7 days, interval=12h..36h whole hours from its start time, but hours drift against a seasonal dusk or dawn, so days suit a nightly or daily rhythm; once the wait is over it stays a candidate until it starts, so a lost chance or a higher prio doesn't roll a new wait, and an admin start counts as a start), weather=rain, snow, storm, fog or clear, tempmin=0 and tempmax=30 (degrees C), chance=50. A list such as moon=full,new holds when any item does. Timing: at=HH:MM starts it later in its night or day, and for=phase (the default), 2p (phases), 6h or 3.5d sets how long it lasts. prio=10: when several events qualify, the highest is tried first. Effects: speed, steps, health, rise, wake, off, set., say, color, sound and the sky (sky, fogcolor, fog, desat, dark, ambient), as in Day and Night, with grow= for its own ranges; a moon starts from Night and a sun from Day except for say, color and sound, and a range it takes from them grows with their grow=. Players' games get its sky with the next climate update, up to about 10 in-game minutes after it starts, and fade it in; admin climate overrides win, and view distance can't change. One event runs at a time, and nothing else is decided while it runs. An event with an error is skipped and logged. Keep each option under 32000 bytes.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Events2_tooltip: More events, written as in Events 1. The option an event is in only matters between events with the same prio: earlier ones are tried first.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Events3_tooltip: More events, written as in Events 1. The option an event is in only matters between events with the same prio: earlier ones are tried first.

Sandbox_Crepuscular_Kinds_tooltip: Monsters of other mods, told by their outfit: name=prefix,prefix;name=prefix, for example wraiths=ZW_,Wraith;husks=Husk_. A zombie whose outfit name starts with one of the prefixes (upper and lower case don't matter) belongs to that kind. Names are made of a-z, 0-9 and _. cof (Cry of Fear Monster NPCs) and mutants (The Mutants) are built in, and other mods can add kinds of their own. Put a kind in off= of Day, Night or an event to remove its far members while that applies; it can't keep a mod from turning zombies into its monsters. When The Mutants is loaded, members of every kind are never turned into mutants.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_KeepDistance_tooltip: While a kind is off, a member of it is removed only if it has no target and no player is within this many tiles of it, in a straight line. 0 to 300. Keep it beyond what players can see, or monsters vanish in view.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RemovalsPerMinute_to: Most far monsters of kinds that are off removed per in-game minute, all kinds together, 1 to 500. Every player's game is told to remove its copy of each one.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_MutantRequeue_toolti: Only matters when The Mutants is loaded. On: when mutants come back on (the definition in effect no longer has off=mutants), the zombies already loaded are offered to The Mutants, up to 200 per in-game minute, so the ones it picks turn into mutants at once. Some may change in plain view. Off: The Mutants only looks at a zombie when it is next created or loaded.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_ZombiesPerSweep_tool: Zombies checked each in-game minute, 50 to 5000, on the server and on every player's game, for the speed and health of the definition in effect. After a change it takes about the number of loaded zombies divided by this many minutes until every zombie has it; more costs more time each minute.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RiseDelayMin_tooltip: In-game hours, 0 to 48, from a zombie's death until its corpse may get up, if it was marked to rise by the rise= in effect when it died. Each corpse gets a time picked at random between this and Rise after at most. Corpses are checked every 10 in-game minutes, only while the definition in effect has wake=true, and one that rises stands up within seconds; a corpse that comes due at another time waits for one, and a corpse in an area no player has loaded waits until one does.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RiseDelayMax_tooltip: In-game hours, 0 to 48: the latest a marked corpse comes due after its death. Below Rise after at least, the two are swapped and the log warns once; equal to it, every corpse comes due exactly then.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_MaxRises_tooltip: How many times one body can rise, 0 to 20; 0 for no limit. The count goes with the risen zombie until the game unloads it, which it does when the zombie walks out of the loaded area, at every restart and at every load of a single player game: then it is an ordinary zombie again, and its count starts over.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RiseMaxAgeHours_tool: A marked corpse whose zombie died more than this many in-game hours ago stays down, 0 to 8760 (a year); 0 for no limit. A check drops it, and dragging it later doesn't bring it back unless this has been raised or set to 0 since. A corpse that has turned into a skeleton rises as one.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_FireStaysDown_toolti: On: a zombie that dies while burning is never marked to rise. A corpse that burns is gone, so it never rises either way.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_FinishOff_tooltip: On: right-clicking zombie corpses offers Finish off for the one nearest the player, as the game's own corpse options pick one. The player walks up to it and finishes it off, and it never rises again; with several zombie corpses on its tile, it finishes off all of them. It is offered on every zombie corpse, so the menu doesn't show which ones would rise. The server takes it only from a player within 3 tiles of the corpse.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_FinishOffSeconds_too: How long Finish off takes, in seconds at normal game speed, 1 to 30.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_HeadHitsStayDown: Floor head hits keep zombies down
Sandbox_Crepuscular_HeadHitsStayDown_too: Experimental. On: a zombie that dies within 5 seconds of a melee hit to its head while it lay on the floor stays down. Only the attacker's own game knows where a hit landed, so it reports the hit, and the server takes the report only from a player within 3 tiles of the zombie. Standing head hits and firearms don't count.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RiseInSafehouses_too: Off: a corpse that would rise inside a claimed safehouse stays down instead. On: it rises like any other.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RisePlayers_tooltip: On: a zombie that was a player can be marked to rise when it is killed, like any other. Off: it stays down.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RiseKinds_tooltip: Monster kinds whose killed members can be marked to rise too, written as in off=: for example cof,mutants, or a kind of the Monster kinds option. Empty: only ordinary zombies rise. Bandits never rise. A monster rises as any corpse does, in the same outfit; what it can do after that is up to its own mod. A list that isn't kind names separated by commas is logged and no monster rises; a name that isn't a known kind is logged too.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RisesPerScan_tooltip: Most corpses that rise in one check, every 10 in-game minutes, on the whole server, 1 to 100; a check searches around for at most five times this many corpses that aren't where they died, and the rest wait for the next. Corpses in areas no player has loaded wait without using this up.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_RiserLimit_tooltip: Most marked corpses kept waiting to rise, 100 to 50000; above it the oldest is dropped and stays down, even if it is dragged later.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Notifications_toolti: On: when a definition begins, every player sees its line (say=) and hears its sound (sound=), and so does a player who joins or loads the game while it is in effect; turning this on shows the line and sound of the definition in effect at once. Off: no player sees or hears any of them, and the events still run as before. Admins still get the replies of the Crepuscular menu and the line about definitions with errors.
Sandbox_Crepuscular_Verbose_tooltip: Writes phase changes, each decision with its rolls, event starts and ends, sandbox value changes, removals of far monsters and mutant requeues to the log, prefixed [Crepuscular]. Warnings and errors, such as mistakes in the definitions, are always logged.
